subject: [Proposal] Commit tiering, throughput acceptance criteria, and discount framing
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Tran <alice@syncai.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Draft: commit tiering & throughput acceptance criteria

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation, attaching a first-pass pricing matrix that ties reserved commit bands to expected GPU pool sizing and the throughput guarantees you care about. High-level callouts:

- We propose three commit tiers for SyncAI: Standard, Performance, and Enterprise. Each maps to a reserved monthly token throughput and a target GPU pool size to meet that throughput.
- Throughput guarantees are expressed as sustained tokens/sec across your dedicated pool (not per-GPU). We also include requests/sec guidance for typical small-chat vs long-generation mixes.
- Acceptance testing: we run a mutually observed 2-hour validation window (test harness attached). The acceptance criterion is that 95% of 1-minute buckets meet or exceed the committed tokens/sec and 95th percentile latency targets for your workload.

I've attached the pricing matrix and the throughput test plan (pdf). Would you be able to confirm which commit tier you'd like priced as an annual reserved commit? Happy to walk through the measurement methodology if your procurement or infra teams want to join.

Next steps we suggested:
1) You confirm target tier (or expected peak tokens/day).
2) We schedule a 30–60 minute technical benchmark run with your sample prompts (we'll bring the harness).
3) Post-run we finalize the contract SLA language for tokens/sec guarantees and crediting.

Cheers,
Ben

Subject: Re: Draft: commit tiering & throughput acceptance criteria

Ben —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and attachments. A few clarifying questions from our side before we pick a tier:

1) How do you compute tokens/sec when we have a mixed workload? Our mix is roughly 60% short chat (avg 50 tokens output), 30% summarization (avg 400 tokens), 10% long-runs (avg 2,500 tokens).
2) What are the latency tiers you guarantee for small/chat requests vs long runs? We can't tolerate >200ms p95 on short chat.
3) If we exceed committed throughput for short bursts, how are bursts handled? Any auto-burst capacity or overage pricing?

Procurement is also asking if we can get a single-year commit with an upfront payment in exchange for an expanded discount; what's the largest discount you can offer on a 12-month prepay at the Performance tier?

—Alice

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-30T12:00:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: SyncAI questions — need numbers + legal angles

Team — forwarding SyncAI's clarifying questions. Please see inline answers below and propose a pricing/discount counter we can send today. Key asks: mixed-workload tokens/sec calc, p95 latency target for short-chat (Alice asked <=200ms), burst behavior, and max prepay discount at Performance tier.

My preliminary thoughts: we can define a tokens/sec effective conversion using weighted average token cost based on their mix; propose guaranteeing against a weighted sustained tokens/sec target. Bursts handled by a small buffer (burst pool) up to 15% sustained over 5 minutes; beyond that overage billing. For prepay discount, I think 12–15% at Performance with annual prepay is doable, 18–22% for Enterprise if they commit 2x Performance. Need engineering to confirm the burst approach and acceptable latency SLOs.

Ben
-----
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-30T13:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: SyncAI questions — need numbers + legal angles

Ben/Rishi —

Suggested framework to reply with (engineering validated):

1) Mixed-workload tokens/sec: compute an "effective sustained tokens/sec" by converting request mix into tokens/sec demand over a 60-minute moving window. Example using SyncAI mix (60/30/10) and expected per-request token outputs you provided:
   - Short chat: 60% * 50 tokens = 30 tokens per request weighted
   - Summarization: 30% * 400 = 120 tokens per request weighted
   - Long-run: 10% * 2500 = 250 tokens per request weighted
   - If their RPS is X, tokens/sec = X * (30+120+250)/average_latency_seconds — but easier: we recommend they provide expected RPS per class; we can also run synthetic to return an effective tokens/sec.

2) Latency targets:
   - Short-chat (<=50 token generation): p95 <= 180ms (we can commit to 200ms p95 in contract for the Performance tier if they use recommended batching settings).
   - Summarization (avg 400 tokens): p95 <= 650ms.
   - Long-run (2500 tokens): best-effort; SLA tied to throughput, not absolute latency. We guarantee tail behavior at the pool level via routing and queuing policies.

3) Bursting & overage:
   - Burst buffer: 15% of committed tokens/sec available for 5-minute windows.
   - Sustained >15% for longer than 5 minutes triggers overage billing at a per-token rate.

4) Measurement methodology (short version):
   - Mutually observed 2-hour run. Pre-populate KV/prefix cache with warm input set.
   - Run with their real prompt mix scripted; collect 1-minute buckets for tokens/sec and p95 latencies.
   - Acceptance: at least 95% of 1-minute buckets meet/exceed the committed tokens/sec and p95 latency targets.

5) Pricing/discount guidance:
   - Performance tier (baseline suggested for SyncAI): maps to a 1.25M tokens/sec pool (estimated 10 A100-equivalent GPUs depending on model size/quantization).
   - Prepay discount: 12% on annual prepay for Performance; 18% available for Enterprise with a 24-month commit.

Legal/contract note (Marissa): will need explicit measurement appendix and an SLA credits table (e.g., % credits for missed monthly throughput availability bands).

LMK if you want me to draft the pricing rows to send to Alice.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

-----
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-30T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: SyncAI questions — need numbers + legal angles

Confirming Lauren's numbers — engineering validated with infra:
- Performance tier -> target 1.25M tokens/sec sustained across pool. Measured on our reference small-parameter model and adjusted for their model family via our onboarding run.
- Mapping to GPUs: estimate 8–12 A100-equivalent GPUs depending on model and quantization. We'll supply the exact math in the attached pricing spreadsheet.
- Latency: we can commit to p95 <= 200ms for short-chat under the Performance tier if they adopt our recommended batching (client-side tokens-per-request cap of 128) and warm prefixes.
- Bursting: 15% for 5-minute windows as Lauren noted. If they require higher burst headroom we can offer a burst add-on (flat monthly fee + metered overage).

I'll help finalize the numbers for Ben to send. Suggest the following counterproposal to procurement:
- Performance annual prepay: 12% discount on list price.
- Performance annual prepay + 30% growth commitment (committed growth path in year 2) -> 16% discount.
- Enterprise (2x Performance commit): 20% discount for 24-month prepay.

Rishi
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Alice / SyncAI procurement —

Thanks for the quick clarifying questions. Attached is a concise summary tailored to SyncAI with the Performance-tier numbers and measurement steps. Highlights:

- Committed throughput: 1,250,000 tokens/sec sustained across dedicated pool.
- Latency: short-chat p95 target <= 200ms (conditioned on client-side cap 128 tokens/generation and pre-populated prefix cache).
- Burst policy: 15% buffer for 5 minutes; overage billed thereafter.
- Measurement: mutually observed 2-hour test; acceptance = 95% of 1-minute buckets meeting tokens/sec and p95 latency.
- Pricing: Performance annual prepay = list -12% (12% discount) — pricing rows in attached spreadsheet.
- Optional: upgrade to Enterprise (2x capacity) for 20% discount on 24-month prepay; or Performance + committed 30% growth path -> 16% discount.

If that framing looks good, can we schedule the validation run next week? Please confirm availability for a 2-hour window and share a sample of 100 representative prompts (we'll keep these private and only use them for the run).

Best,
